values: SWRL rules over observations assign alarm levels from alarm ranges attached to observable properties, and combine nearby alarms with custom geo built-ins.

Own classes declared equivalent to SOSA ones (ucsn:DataValue to sosa:Observation, ucsn:SensedInformation to sosa:ObservableProperty), with a sensing status per property recording sharing with data consumers; past locations of mobile sensors.
The feature of interest is a node per property and location (tempFOI/location/001); about 80 to 90 triples per observation.
Queries mint terms in the sosa: namespace (sosa:PointID, sosa:Temperature, sosa:MuseumPoint) and attach sosa:hasResult directly to properties (udeo:availableBikeNumber sosa:hasResult ?x).

Observations subclassed per modality (TimeSeriesObservation, ImageObservation, ComputedObservation derivedFrom sources); SWRL rules compare simple results with specification limits bound to the same observable property; DetectionMethod subclasses sosa:Procedure.
Own foo: copies of SOSA classes aligned by owl:equivalentClass; observable properties double as datatype properties carrying values; trail-camera images given by a path URI.

Access permissions are attached to observable and actuatable properties rather than to observations; ssn-system property subclasses carry values via dul:hasDataValue; observation quality as subclasses (Poor, Fair, Good).
madeLastObservation is a subproperty of sosa:madeObservation for the latest result; sosa:hosts relates appliances to ingredients they contain; SWRL rules pick the actuator for a cooking step.
Features of interest are locations (station site, hypocentre); a data point has one to three axis components; collections of collections (matrix of arrays).

Observations subclassed per theme (kwg-ont:VulnerabilityObservation); census and survey statistics modelled as observations of regions and S2 cells; integration through the spatial feature rather than shared properties.

Each observable property declares the observation type it takes as value (semic:observationType), observations are subclassed per type (occupancy observations), and static properties hold literal values.

Observations are also ewe:Events, actuations ewe:Actions and results ewe:Parameters (task automation); one property class is a subclass of both ObservableProperty and ActuatableProperty; actuators use sosa:forProperty.
Observations subclassed by epistemic level (EvidenceObservation, PerceivedHazardObservation, PropertyEstimation); reliability attached to results; revisable estimated event states with OWL-Time.

Own ofo: copy of the sensor pattern (Wearable, Feedback, Property, FeatureOfInterest) aligned to SOSA; results may attach to feedback, property or feature; time series stay in InfluxDB behind data points.
Quality-of-context criteria and min/max interpretation thresholds are attached to observable properties.
Sensor functions are sosa:Procedures with ssn:Input/ssn:Output arguments; SHACL metadata profiles validate every node; system parameters are ssn:Property of components.
The feature of interest is a location node (location/001); about 80 to 90 triples per observation.
Stations are subclasses of both sosa:Platform and geo:Feature; an interpolator ssn:System is hosted on grid-cell platforms; the graph is virtual (Ontop mappings over SQL).

Observations are subclassed per kind (SpatialPositionObservation, SafetyDistanceObservation from 3D simulation, CVPeopleNumObservation from video AI) and sosa:Observation is itself a subclass of ctx:ExternalContext; quantities are separate qudt:Quantity nodes with unit:KiloGM.
Queries use 2011 SSN terms (observedBy, observationResultTime, hasValue) under the 2017 ssn: namespace, with iot-lite for quantity kinds and devices.

Feature, phenomenon time and provenance (raster file) sit on the collection, members carry only property and result; collections are also dcat:Dataset and prov:Entity; feature is a version of a territorial parcel.
A storm track is a collection of tracklet collections, each tracklet a sample point with time, location and observed attributes; damage types are observed properties of storm events.
An elephant's GPS position is modelled as the result of an observation of an invented sosa:Location property.
2011 SSN with measurement capabilities (accuracy, sensitivity as rdf:value) per device; dynamic properties such as the last measure attached directly to the sensor resource.
2011 SSN with iot-lite: ssn:Device subdivided into sensing and actuating devices; medical objects contain devices and carry own has-location and has-time properties.
A knowledge graph merging 2011 SSN and SOSA terms, choosing ssn:Property over sosa:ObservableProperty as the property class.
Only class alignments between ontologies (SSN/SOSA Sensor, Procedure and FeatureOfInterest made equivalent to OEMA, OntoWind and SAREF classes); no instance data shown.
SWRL-style rules classify observations into derived classes (TrustedObservations, ObservationToHighLevelEnergy) and attach trust values to entities.
SAREF and SOSA combined: measurements subclassed per quantity (IndoorTemperatureMeasurement) carry sosa:hasSimpleResult; SWRL rules compare them with occupants' comfort settings to set actuators.
Per-quantity object properties (hasTemperature, hasPressure, hasWindForce, belongsObservation) and value data properties replace the generic observedProperty pattern.
MQTT packets mapped to SOSA terms: grip position and correction points as properties, actuation signals with correction offsets as simple results.

Readings below the threshold are not stored, so the collection carries aggregate statistics (average, count); constraint evaluations (EP-Plan) are based on the collection; observations are also prov:Activity.
SOSA, QUDT and D-SI terms used as keys of JSON metadata attached to HDF5-style data groups, with madeBySensor pointing to a string.
Calibrated sensors carry a dynamic transfer model whose parameters have units and uncertainties, with covariance matrices encoded in MathML.

SOSA/SSN reduced to a flat event-log schema: observable and actuatable properties merged into one Property, Platform and Deployment merged into a Location concept, feature of interest replaced by the business object of the OCEL log.
The patient wearing a sensor is modelled as the platform that hosts it; situations detected by C-SPARQL aggregates over windows.
sosa:hosts/isHostedBy inside WoT Thing Descriptions drive the URI hierarchy of Solid pod containers.
The IoT-Stream extension adds stream entities between sensors and observations for search and indexing.
Observations are typed per quantity with a class minted in the sosa: namespace (sosa:HeartRateObservation); no observedProperty is given.
SOSA/SSN names reused as annotation values in an XES event-log extension (system type, interaction type), with sosa:Sampling read as a set of subsequent observations.
Observations produced by RML mappings from JSON outputs of ML anomaly-detection modules.
2011 SSN output/value pattern (SensorOutput, ObservationValue, isProducedBy) specialised per quantity (TrafficIntensity...).
The feature of interest is a location node whose IRI encodes the coordinates (oim-feat:loc_70.41_0.0).
The query links sensors to observations with sosa:observes instead of madeObservation; unit heterogeneity (bar, hectopascal) resolved at query time.
Calibrated-sensor classes combine SOSA with the digital SI model (D-SI) for measurement uncertainty and calibration models.
An RL agent annotates environment streams with SSN observations of process properties (waiting time of an order).
Factorized observations: identical readings at different timestamps are represented once, to shrink the knowledge graph built on demand from a stream.
Observation and its OM measure merged into one instance typed sosa:Observation and om:Measure.
Models written in YAML and converted to N-Quads to generate edge deployments.
sosa:isObservedBy links observations to gateways (the property is meant for observable properties); observations are presence intervals derived from image interpretation.
New sensor types are added as ssn:Sensor subclasses to an IoT dictionary built by knowledge extraction.
N3 rules generate sensor queries; uses a non-SOSA sosa:hasObservation linking a sensor to observations that carry symptoms.
